name: The Dismemberment Plan
label: DeSoto
lede: A D.C. band records its best-known album on Interscope's money, gets dropped in the merger, and watches DeSoto, the label two Jawbox alumni run, put it out anyway.

eras.title: Suburban Virginia to DeSoto
eras.text: Four people from the Virginia suburbs start a band in 1993 and land on DeSoto Records, the D.C. label two Jawbox alumni run. The first drummer leaves after the debut, and the lineup that lasts arrives.

years.h: Named for an insurance plan in Groundhog Day
years.p: [[Travis Morrison|b9ba9319-c5c7-4316-b32a-d3f92a673e1f]], [[Eric Axelson|ecc42a4f-e214-40f1-af6d-6cdcade19702]], Jason Caddell and Steve Cummings start the band in D.C.; three of them went to Lake Braddock Secondary School in Burke, Virginia.
years.xp: The name comes from a scene in the 1993 film Groundhog Day in which an insurance policy called the dismemberment plan gets a mention. Cummings, Morrison and Caddell had gone to school together in Burke, Virginia, and Axelson also attended Lake Braddock.

years.h: The first record is an EP called Can We Be Mature?
years.p: It lands a year ahead of the first full album.

years.h: ! gets the band onto DeSoto
years.p: DeSoto Records puts out the debut. Steve Cummings leaves afterward and Joe Easley takes over on drums.
years.xp: Easley takes the drums in 1995 and stays for the rest of the band's run. From here on it's Morrison, Caddell, Axelson and Easley.

eras.title: Terrified, then signed to a major
eras.text: A second album gets the majors calling and Interscope signs the band for two. Three weeks in a New Jersey studio on that budget produce the record the band is remembered for, and the label that paid for it won't be around to release it.

years.h: The Dismemberment Plan Is Terrified gets the majors calling
years.p: The second album on DeSoto, jumpier and funnier than the debut.

years.src: Wikipedia: Emergency & I · PopMatters: Emergency & I at 25
years.h: Major-label money, then a merger
years.p: Interscope signs the band to a two-album deal. Seagram buys PolyGram in May 1998, and the label's world rearranges.
years.xp:
Universal then folded Geffen and A&M into Interscope, which is how a two-album deal for a D.C. indie band ended up inside a company restructuring around it.

PopMatters has the band on the Interscope roster through 1998 and 1999, recording Emergency & I on the label's budget.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Dismemberment Plan · PopMatters: Emergency & I at 25
yt: The Ice of Boston, live on KEXP (2013)
years.h: One Interscope release, and it's an EP
years.p: Wikipedia's account says The Ice of Boston repackages a track. PopMatters hears it pointing toward Emergency & I.
years.xp: According to the band's Wikipedia entry, the EP was the only item Interscope released during the deal. PopMatters says it "points the way forward" with a mix of humor, isolation and a big chorus.

eras.title: Dropped, then released anyway
eras.text: The label that paid for the record is gone before it can put it out. DeSoto releases it, and it becomes the record the band gets remembered for.

years.big: "I'm glad we got dropped, it's not sour grapes."
q: It was kind of scary because we didn't know if we were going to get it back.
years.src: Wikipedia: Emergency & I · Chip Midnight: The Dismemberment Plan (2000) · Vice: Looking Back on Change
yt: Live at the Blue Room, Chico, April 18, 1999
years.h: Dropped, with $50,000 for the trouble
years.p: They learn in April 1999, on tour with [[Burning Airlines|5ea472eb-5040-410c-b021-1e678276aed9]], that they're among the acts cut after the Universal merger.
years.xp:
Wikipedia reports the band received $50,000 owed on the second album of the deal. Axelson told Chip Midnight that everyone they had dealt with at the label was gone by then, and that the scary part was whether they'd get the record back at all.

They did. Vice reports Interscope handed over the masters as a parting gift, and the band came out with a finished record, no debt and DeSoto ready to release it.

years.h: The City is already a live song by February 6, 1999
years.p: The footage predates both the album and the Interscope cut.

years.h: Emergency & I comes out on DeSoto after all
years.p: Interscope's budget paid for it; a label run out of D.C. by two ex-Jawbox members puts it out.
years.xp:
Main tracking was three weeks at Water Music in Hoboken, New Jersey, with more work at Inner Ear Studios in Arlington, Virginia; [[J. Robbins|3babd931-a940-43a8-b629-d7aed5b821d9]] and [[Chad Clark|f3f09e99-e31c-4aa2-99e4-0b4e59e72f87]] produced, per Wikipedia. Morrison made the cover art on a computer at Water Music between sessions.

Pitchfork's Brent DiCrescenzo gave it 9.6 out of 10 and told readers to buy it right away. In 2011 the site raised the score to 10 for the Barsuk vinyl reissue.

years.src: Washington City Paper: [Your Band] Played Here
years.h: Two nine-foot costumes turn up at Fort Reno
years.p: A Pikachu and a box labeled Box of Pubes, both from Baltimore, come to the band's 1999 free show in Fort Reno Park.
years.xp: David Arbury tells the Washington City Paper's Fort Reno oral history that two guys came in nine-foot costumes, one in a tall box with a hole for his face, inspired by a recent Conan O'Brien sketch. Axelson's take: "people would come to Plan shows and make it their own."

eras.title: Opening for Pearl Jam, then a darker record
eras.text: Three weeks across Europe as an opener, then an album slower and darker than the last. Morrison says he heard the wheels coming off the band halfway through writing it.

years.cap: Bass and guitar on stage, July 28, 2000
years.h: The Pearl Jam email leads Morrison to an Indian restaurant
years.p: Morrison calls the number in the email from Pearl Jam's management and gets a restaurant. The offer is real: three weeks of European dates, starting June 14 in Prague.
years.xp:
The email, as Axelson relays it to Chip Midnight: "They got your CD, they like it, they came see you on the West Coast." The tour ran June 14 to July 3.

Some of the festival dates were in fields holding tens of thousands, with the band on early in the day. The biggest crowd they'd played before that was around a thousand, at HFS-Fest in D.C., opening for Veruca Salt.

years.src: Wikipedia: Change · Vice: Looking Back on Change
years.h: Change gets made at Inner Ear, with J. Robbins
years.p: Morrison says it's slower, darker and more gothic than Emergency & I. Pitchfork names it 14th album of 2001.
years.xp:
Robbins engineered and Clark mixed. Morrison told Vice it sounds "like postcards from the edge of thirty, thematically," and that its melodrama no longer bothers him: "Melodrama happens."

He has said he can hear the Pearl Jam tour in the heavier songs, naming Time Bomb and Secret Curse, and that he heard the wheels coming off the band halfway through writing.

eras.title: A farewell made of requests
eras.text: The new songs aren't exciting anyone, so the band stops. The send-off ends with two hours of fan requests at the 9:30 Club.

years.big: "We don't know how to make a record unless we can write music that excites us."
years.src: Washington City Paper: What Do You Want Them to Say? · Perfect Sound Forever: Travis Morrison · Wikipedia: The Dismemberment Plan
years.h: The new songs aren't working, so the band stops
years.p: Caddell explains the breakup to the Washington City Paper. The announcement comes January 19, 2003, after more than 800 shows.
years.xp:
What the band was writing wasn't doing that, and Caddell said so plainly. A farewell run called One Last Slice followed.

The band posted individual tracks online for fans to remix; the results came out as A People's History of the Dismemberment Plan.

years.src: Washington City Paper: [Your Band] Played Here · Wikipedia: The Dismemberment Plan
years.h: Lightning ends the last Fort Reno show early
years.p: Axelson remembers getting through about eight songs before rain and gear trouble stopped it.
years.xp: Axelson tells the Washington City Paper's oral history: "We got off maybe eight songs and fucked up some gear...there was lightning, and it was not a safe thing for us to be doing." Wikipedia lists the July 28 show as cancelled; the oral history has them playing a partial set.

years.cap: Playing The Ice of Boston at the Bowery Ballroom, New York, July 23, 2003
years.src: Perfect Sound Forever: Travis Morrison · Washington City Paper: What Do You Want Them to Say? · Washingtonian: Travis Morrison on Reuniting · Wikipedia: The Dismemberment Plan
years.h: The farewell at the 9:30 Club is almost all requests
years.p: A sold-out room gets about two hours of what it asked for.
years.xp:
The September 1 show made up for the rained-out Fort Reno date. Perfect Sound Forever calls it an unheard-of two hours of nearly all requests.

Morrison, in Washingtonian: "We very rarely sold shows out and we never sold them out in advance except for the last one."

eras.title: A zero, a new band, and a benefit
eras.text: Morrison's solo album gets a zero from Pitchfork, Axelson starts Maritime, and one weekend at the Black Cat sells out in minutes.

years.h: Travistan draws a 0.0 from Pitchfork
years.p: Morrison's first solo record gets a zero from the site that scored Emergency & I 9.6.
years.xp: It came out on Barsuk. Perfect Sound Forever reports many independent record stores stopped stocking it, and describes the score as one the site was said to have avoided repeating. Morrison later fronted a band called the Hellfighters and moved to New York.

years.h: Axelson starts Maritime with ex-members of the Promise Ring
years.p: Glass Floor is the first Maritime album, in 2004; two more follow in 2006 and 2007.

years.cap: The band at the first of their 2007 reunion shows
years.src: Washingtonian: Travis Morrison on Reuniting · Washington City Paper: What Do You Want Them to Say?
yt: You Are Invited, Black Cat, April 28, 2007
years.h: A benefit at the Black Cat sells out in four minutes
years.p: Two nights, April 27 and 28, raise money for Callum Robbins, son of [[J. Robbins|3babd931-a940-43a8-b629-d7aed5b821d9]].
years.xp:
Morrison to Washingtonian: "We knew they would sell out, but not in four minutes." He said the band had known when it broke up that it would want to do something like this some day, and that they were "much bigger and more popular now after we broke up than ever before."

The Washington City Paper says the show sold out so fast another was added.

eras.title: The reunion that stuck
eras.text: A vinyl reissue turns into shows, the shows turn into a tour, and the tour turns into a new album.

years.src: Wikipedia: Emergency & I · Wikipedia: The Dismemberment Plan · Washington City Paper: What Do You Want Them to Say?
years.h: The Washington Post says the band will play again
years.p: Axelson says there are no plans for a new record, only shows.
years.xp:
The shows were tied to the Barsuk vinyl reissue of Emergency & I, which followed on January 11, 2011 with four bonus tracks and oral-history liner notes.

Caddell told the Washington City Paper that playing again "shocked the band into an awareness that we didn't have before."

years.src: Atomic Ned: The Dismemberment Plan was on TV
years.h: The City goes out on Late Night with Jimmy Fallon
years.p: Network TV, during the reissue run.
years.xp: The band played two songs on the show, The City and What Do You Want Me to Say?. Atomic Ned notes only The City had made it to YouTube, and that the U.S. reunion shows were all sold out.

years.cap: Black Cat, Washington, first night of the January 2011 run
years.src: Washington City Paper: What Do You Want Them to Say? · Atomic Ned: The Dismemberment Plan was on TV
years.h: Three Black Cat nights become a summer of festivals
years.p: Ten more dates follow the January shows, including the Pitchfork Music Festival in Chicago and the Roots Picnic in Philadelphia.
years.xp: The Washington City Paper counts 13 shows in all behind the vinyl reissue: three in D.C. in January, the rest on the road.

years.cap: The band, press photo for Uncanney Valley, 2013
years.h: Twelve years after Change, Uncanney Valley
years.p: On Partisan. The single Waiting arrives with a phone number fans can call.
years.xp: The number promoted was 252-64-DPLAN. Singles Waiting, Invisible and Daddy Was a Real Good Dancer came out between July and September.

eras.title: Back to Emergency & I at 25
eras.text: A cover for a Dischord tribute leads into six anniversary shows.

years.h: A Dischord tribute gets the band's take on Circus Lupus
years.p: The cover of Unrequited was recorded in August 2023, a nod to the D.C. scene that raised them.

years.h: Twenty-five years on, Emergency & I goes back on the road
years.p: Dates include Best Friends Forever in Las Vegas and United Sounds in New York.
